spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @b14d8c4e (design rulings at b14d8c4e; 376f47f1 added design shard and the planner, implementer and assayer positions; source identical to f2cd7e3a): plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability`, and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize the ruled `design stability` in the design skill: the design is the fixed target while a plan realizes it; a change bearing on a shard a running plan builds against is held as a note until that plan completes, then enters the design and is realized by a following plan, sequenced after the work it depends on; a change to any other part of the design enters at once; only when a running plan is found built on a shard that is itself wrong does the plan stop, the design is corrected once, and the planner rectifies or rebuilds the plan before work resumes. At census packages/canon/src/skills/design/skill.ts says `yield ≠ ∅ ⇒ amend(C) ⟨intake at INCEPTION ∧ live, never at retirement …⟩`, amending at once whatever plan stands on the concept, and nothing says how a plan stops or resumes; deliver's `finding ⇒ fold ≺ self's next dispatch` (removed by deliver-loop) does the same mid-plan. The plan-side half (the planner re-plans, drift of a bound plan answered then) is unit planner-position's, in plan/skill.ts.
THE LOOP (the contract each workflow unit of this plan states its own share of; the design states what must hold and why, this is how). (1) The architect cuts the design into shards (a shard is one concept with everything it stands on, stating what and why, never how) and hands a set of them to the planner. The planner plans them (units each realizing one shard, dependencies first, each sized for one implementer, how each shard is realized on each harness included), binds the plan when no plan is bound, records each ready unit active as it hands it out, and returns only the plan's name and those units' names. (2) The architect routes each name, by name alone, to one implementer, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address `<unit> of <plan>` and nothing it wrote itself; a unit's name is an address the architect never reads behind. Delegates are named so they can be messaged again (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch, nested dispatch allowed; omp: agent messaging). (3) The implementer reads its unit's spec alone (never the design), builds on its own branch, proves only what its spec asks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that name to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; a finding it meets it captures as a note. (4) The architect routes the name and commit to the assayer. The assayer reads the shard and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. It is the one judge of a unit. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect routes the name and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec and returns `whole <unit> of <plan>`, which the architect routes to the planner; the planner records the unit completed and hands out the newly ready names as in (1). Red or a merge conflict: the line is left as it was and it returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. The integrator never repairs, never judges and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed the planner closes the plan; the architect routes that to the integrator, which asks the operator to release the line to main (a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command). It never moves main. (8) The architect never reads a unit's spec (`plan show <unit>`), a plan view, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. What reaches it is names (from the planner and on verdicts and results), verdicts, the integrator's red naming a unit, and notes. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice; every delegate's finding reaches it as a note. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing, amended into the design only after that plan closes, and realized by a following plan; a change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the bound plan is found built on a shard that is itself wrong does the architect stop it: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds the plan; then the architect retracts the note and work resumes.
Because the held change never amends a running plan's shard, the head the plan's units pin stays the only head, the assayer reads exactly the shard the unit was built for, and the runtime, `pin` and `view` need no change.
CHANGE. (1) design/skill.ts (after design-shard's edit in wave 0) states (9): the `yield ≠ ∅ ⇒ amend(C)` law becomes: every input, the operator's included, and every delegate's finding (a note, per the design) is a hypothesis self rectifies; a surviving change bearing on a shard a bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note blocking nothing and amended when that plan completes, for a following plan; any other change is amended at once; a wrong shard under a bound plan: capture a note blocking the plan, amend once, the planner re-plans, retract the note. The description says so in one clause. Declare no new symbol another cell declares differently (bind with `@ home`), so symbol-altitude.test.ts stays green without its ledger, which this unit does not own.
(2) .changeset/design-stability.md (@cratylus/canon minor). No new test file.
